div.head: I As Prol.
div.ab: Æðelstan cyningc, mid geþeahte Wulfhelm arcebiscop ⁊ eac minra oðera biscopa, cyð ðam gerefan to hwilcere birig ⁊ eow bidde on Godes naman ⁊ on eallum his haligra ⁊ eac be minum freondscipe, þæt ge ærest of minum agenum gode agifan ða teoðunga, ægðer ge on cwicum ceape ge on ðæs geares eorðwæstmum, swa man rihtost mage oððe gemetan oððe getellan oððe awegan; ⁊ þa biscopas þonne þæt ilce don on heora agenum gode, ⁊ mine ealdormen ⁊ mine gerefan þæt silfe.

Ic Æþelstan cyng, mid geþehte Wulfhelmes arcebiscopes ⁊ eac minra oþerra biscopa, cyþe þam gerefan to gehwylcere byrig ⁊ eow bidde on Godes naman ⁊ on ealra his haligra ⁊ eac be minum freondscipe beode, þæt ge ærest of minum agenum góde agyfan þa teoþunga, ægþer ge on cwicum ceape ge on þæs geares eorðwæstmum, swa man rihtast mæge oððe gemetan oððe getellan oððe awegan; ⁊ þa biscopas þonne þæt ylce don on heora agenum gode, ⁊ mine ealdormen ⁊ mine gerefan þæt sylfe.

Ic Æþelstane cyning, mid geþeahte Wulfhelmes mines hehbisceopes ⁊ oþra minra bisceopa, bebeode eallum minum gereafum ðurh ealle mine rice on þæs Drihtænes nama ⁊ ealra halgena ⁊ for mine lufu, þæt hi ærost mines agenes æhtes ðam teoþe gesyllaþ, ge ðæs libbēdes yrfes ge ðæs gearlices westmes; ⁊ þæt ilce gedó eac ða bisceopas heora gehwylera ⁊ eac mine ealdormanna ⁊ gereafa.

Ego Æþelstanus rex, consilio Wulfhelmes archiepiscopi mei et aliorum episcoporum meorum, mando prepositis meis omnibus in toto regno meo et precipio in nomine Domini et sanctorum omnium et super amicitiam meam, ut in primis de meo proprio reddant Deo decimas utriusque in uiuente captali et in ornotinis frugibus terre; et episcopi (mei) similiter faciant de suo proprio et aldermanni mei et prepositi mei.

Ic Æþelstan cyng, mid geþehte Wulfhelmes [mines] arcebiscopes ⁊ eac minra oþerra biscopa, cyþe þam gerefan to gehwylcere byrig ⁊ eow bidde on Godes naman ⁊ on ealra his haligra ⁊ eac be minum freondscipe beode, þæt ge ærest of minum agenum góde agyfan þa teoþunga, ægþer ge on cwicum ceape ge on þæs geares eorðwæstmum, swa man rihtast mæge oððe gemetan oððe getellan oððe awegan; ⁊ þa biscopas þonne þæt ylce don on heora agenum gode, ⁊ mine ealdormen ⁊ mine gerefan þæt sylfe.

Ic Æðelstan cyng, mid geþehte Wulfhelmes arcebiscopes and eac minra oþerra biscopa, cyðe þam gerefan to gehwylcere byrig and eow bidde on Godes naman and on ealra his haligra, and eac be minum freondscipe beode, þæt ge ærest of minum agenum gode agyfan þa teoþunga, ægþer ge on cwicum ceape ge on þæs geares eorðwæstmum, swa man rihtast mæge oððe gemetan oððe getellan oððe awegan. And þa biscopas þonne þæt ylce don on heora agenum gode, and mine ealdormen and mine gerefan þæt sylfe.

Ich, König Aethelstan, mit Beirath (meines lq) Erzbischofs Wulfhelm und auch meiner anderen Bischöfe, künde den (allen meinen lq) Gerichtsvögten in jeder Stadt (durch mein ganzes Reich hin lq) im Namen Gottes (des Herrn lq) und aller seiner Heiligen und auch bei meiner Freundschaft (aus Liebe zu mir Ld) gebiete ich, dass ihr (sie lq) erstens von meinem eigenen Gute die Zehnten gebet (zahlen lq), sowohl am Lebgute wie an des Jahres Erdfrüchten (vom lebenden Vieh wie von der jährlichen Frucht Ld), wie man genauestens abmessen oder abzählen oder abwiegen kann; und dasselbe sollen dann (auch lq) die Bischöfe an ihrem eigenen Gute (jeder von ihnen Ld) und meine Ealdormen und Vögte dasselbe thun.

I, King Æthelstan, with the counsel of (my, lq) Archbishop Wulfhelm and also of my other bishops, make known to the (all my, lq) reeves in every town (throughout my whole kingdom, lq), in the name of God (the Lord, lq) and of all his saints, and also by my friendship (out of love for me, Ld) I command that you (they, lq) first of all give (pay, lq) the tithes from my own property, both of live stock and of the year's fruits of the earth (of the living cattle and of the yearly crop, Ld), as one can most exactly measure or count or weigh; and the bishops are then (also, lq) to do the same from their own property (each of them, Ld), and my ealdormen and reeves likewise.

I, King Æthelstan, with the advice of my Archbishop, Wulfhelm, and my other bishops also, inform the reeve in every borough, and pray you in the name of God and of all His saints, and command you also by my friendship, that in the first place ye render tithes of my own property, both in livestock and in the yearly fruits of the earth, measuring, counting and weighing [them] in accordance with the strictest accuracy. And the bishops shall do the same with their own property, and my ealdormen and my reeves likewise.

I, King Æthelstan, with the advice of Archbishop Wulfhelm and also my other bishops, proclaim to the reeves in every community and command you in the name of God and all of his saints, and charge you likewise by my friendship, that you first pay the tithes from my own holdings, both from the livestock and from the year’s produce, seeing that they are measured, counted, and weighed to the best of your ability. And let the bishops do likewise with their holdings, and my ealdormen and my reeves with theirs.
div.note: Liebermann prints Ld in bold where it differs; ‘lq’ = what Ld and Quadripartitus have in common. D's ‘Æðelstan cyningc … cyð’ is corrected by Liebermann to ‘Ic Æ… cyðe’ from G, Ld and Quadr.; he also corrects ‘Wulfhelm arcebiscop’ (16th-c. addition) to ‘Wulfhelmes arcebiscopes’ and ‘eallum’ to ‘ealra’, and supplies ‘beode’.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads); Wormald, Making of English Law I, October 2026 (was “925–c.936; before III As (Attenborough)”, now “925–c.936 (Liebermann); before III As (Attenborough); early in the reign, before II As (Wormald)”); AX: pages in Rabin (text / translation), checked against Rabin (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “342”, now “342 / 343”; 1 rows of I As)
Manuscripts: D = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201, p. 53; G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fols. 86v–87v. Æðelstanes gerædnes: Æðelstanes cinyncges gerædnes D

Archbishop Wulfhelm: Wulfhelm served as archbishop of Canterbury from approximately 926 until his death in 941. His prominent role as one of Æthelstan’s advisors and the likelihood that he composed the laws issued in the latter’s name make him perhaps Wulfstan’s most explicit precursor.

‘Sheriffs’ nicht allein; vgl. Gl Vogt 2e. 6. 11 a. b. 12. 16b. Bessere Übs.: ‘in jedem Gericht (s.d. Gl 1b) (Amtsprengel) und bitte euch’; keineswegs bloss Stadtvögte sind gemeint, sondern weitaus in der Mehrzahl staatliche Vögte über ländliche öffentliche Bezirke und königliche über Herrschaftsgüter der Krone. Laut mando et precipio in Q hatte auch lq zwei Verben statt des einen bebeode in Ld (das allerdings bei As für ‘gebieten’ vorkommt); und (ge)cyðan steht gerade in diesem Sinne zu Beginn von As Alm. V As und anderer Erlasse. — Ich halte ‘durch mein Reich hin’ in lq für weniger ursprünglich als das mehr amtstechnische in dg; auch in As Alm steht zwar ‘innerhalb meines Reiches’, aber auch nur durch lq bezeugt

Not only ‘sheriffs’; cf. Gl Vogt 2e. 6. 11 a. b. 12. 16b. A better translation: ‘in every court (see that word in Gl 1b) (official district), and ask you’; by no means are town reeves alone meant, but, in by far the majority of cases, state reeves over rural public districts and royal reeves over the crown’s demesne estates. According to mando et precipio in Q, lq too had two verbs instead of the single bebeode in Ld (which, admittedly, occurs in As for ‘command’); and (ge)cyðan occurs in precisely this sense at the beginning of As Alm. V As and other decrees. — I consider ‘throughout my kingdom’ in lq less original than the more technical official term in dg; As Alm, it is true, also has ‘within my kingdom’, but this too is attested only by lq
D’s eallum rechtfertigt sich nicht etwa durch Ergänzung eines dt. pl. ‘Namen’; vielmehr vgl. Urk. on Godes naman ⁊ on s. Petres ⁊ on s. Paules; a. 909 Bi 622
D’s eallum is not to be justified by, say, supplying a dat. pl. ‘names’; rather, cf. the charter on Godes naman ⁊ on s. Petres ⁊ on s. Paules; a. 909 Bi 622

Vgl. mine lufu, auch As Alm 1; allein ‘um meinetwillen’ (Belege: Tol ler 648a, geradezu nur pro übersetzend) klingt weniger befehlend als: ‘bei [Verlust] meiner Freundschaft’, die Drohung der Huldentziehung, die auch u. 5⁶ steht; s. Gl Gnade 2

Cf. mine lufu, also As Alm 1; but ‘for my sake’ (instances: Toller 648a, simply rendering pro) sounds less commanding than ‘on [pain of losing] my friendship’, the threat of withdrawal of favour, which also occurs below 5⁶; see Gl Gnade 2

Laut Akzents versteht G: ‘Gute’: richtig laut vorl. Z. Auch Q las gode, das er Deo missverstand. Möglicherweise meinte auch D ‘Gott’. Aber Ld setzt æht, ein Synonym zu jenem Sinne, ein; der masc. gen. dazu wird bei Toller Suppl. nur hierher belegt

Judging by the accent, G understands ‘goods’: correctly, to judge from the last line but one. Q too read gode, which he misunderstood as Deo. Possibly D too meant ‘God’. But Ld substitutes æht, a synonym in the former sense; for its masc. gen. Toller Suppl. cites only this passage
Vgl. Gl Zehnt 6. 15a; die 2 Bestandteile sondern auch Af El 38. II Eg 3. — Laut captale . . terrae las Q die Lesart dg ceap . . eorð, wich also hier Hs. l von lq ab
Cf. Gl Zehnt 6. 15a; Af El 38. II Eg 3 also distinguish the 2 components. — Judging by captale . . terrae, Q read the dg reading ceap . . eorð, so that here MS l departed from lq
Statt ‘Eigengut’ sagt II Eg 2 bocland, kaum anderes meinend
Instead of ‘own property’, II Eg 2 says bocland, hardly meaning anything different
In Ld scheint hinter teoðe, ealdormanna, gerefa das -n zu fehlen; ebenso gereafa[n], hio[m] 1; vielleicht ward Horizontale über dem Endvokal übersehen; vgl. zu As Alm Pro²
In Ld the -n seems to be missing after teoðe, ealdormanna, gerefa; likewise gereafa[n], hio[m] 1; perhaps a horizontal stroke over the final vowel was overlooked; cf. note to As Alm Pro²
Archbishop of Canterbury 925—940 (cf. As. Ord. Pr.; II As. Epilogue).

Liebermann translates ‘in jeder Stadt,’ but in his notes he says that it would be better to translate ‘in jedem Gericht (Amtsprengel)’; adding that the reference is not merely to town officials, but in the great majority of cases to public officials in charge of country districts and royal officials in charge of crown estates. The use of the word byrig would seem to imply that primarily the reeves of boroughs with dependent districts are meant—perhaps as the most important of their class. For a general discussion of the borough see Maitland, Domesday Book and Beyond, p. 172 ff. Cf. II As. cap. 13—18 and notes.
